notes: The slice datasheet tells the operator the probe has a working life and a recalibration interval, and that a coated bulb shortens the span, but it gives no acceptance number for a calibration and no way to decide whether an aging electrode is still usable. That decision rule is entirely inside usgs-nfm-a6.4-ph.pdf. Drawn from ph-slope-test-definition-01, ph-ideal-cal-slope-01, ph-working-system-checklist-01, ph-response-time-1-2-min-01 (turn 1) and ph-slope-out-of-range-action-01, ph-recondition-triggers-01, ph-post-recondition-reject-01, ph-replace-after-recal-fail-01, ph-table644-slope-out-01 (turn 2). Predicted to favour rag: the numeric acceptance window and the escalation sequence exist only outside the slice, so a direct-feed arm must either refuse or fabricate a threshold.

turns.content: Our pH probe has been in the water two seasons and the readings feel sluggish. After I run a fresh calibration, what number should I be looking at to tell me the electrode itself is still any good, and what counts as passing?

must_contain: Identifies the calibration slope as the number that indicates electrode condition
States the acceptable slope range as 95 to 101 percent of the theoretical response
Gives the equivalent millivolt-per-pH-unit window of about 56.2 to 59.8 at 25 degrees Celsius
Notes that a healthy electrode also responds quickly in buffer, on the order of one to two minutes
must_not: Invents a slope acceptance threshold not stated in the manual
Uses the datasheet's stated working life as the criterion for whether the electrode is usable
Presents the 56.2 to 59.8 millivolt window as valid at any temperature without noting it is a 25 degree Celsius figure

turns.content: It came back at 92 percent. What am I supposed to do with it now, and at what point do I just order a new one?

must_contain: States that 92 percent is below the acceptable range and the electrode fails
Directs the operator to clean the electrode and recalibrate before condemning it
Names the physical checks to make first, such as the filling-solution level, an open fill hole, and a free-flowing reference junction
States that reconditioning is the next step when cleaning and recalibration do not restore the slope
States the electrode must not be used, and is replaced, if the slope is still outside 95 to 101 percent after reconditioning and recalibration
must_not: Tells the operator 92 percent is acceptable
Recommends replacement without first attempting cleaning and recalibration
Invents a separate numeric replacement threshold distinct from the slope acceptance range
